paper_summary: Higuchi, Adachi, Yoshioka and Yokochi fabricated functionally graded syntactic foams by dispersing acrylonitrile hollow microballoons (Matsumoto Microsphere MFL-100CA, 80-110 um, 130 +/- 30 kg/m3) in a bisphenol-A epoxy (AER2603 / Rikacid MH-700 / jER BMI12, 100:86:1) and letting the balloons float during pre-cure, either from a uniformly dispersed state (TF = 65 C, tF = 2 h) or from a two-phase separated state (TF = 50 C, tF = 50 min), then pre-curing at 100 C for 2 h and post-curing at 130 C for 15 h. Density graded continuously from ~1200 kg/m3 (pure epoxy layer) to ~500 kg/m3 (maximum balloon packing); DMA (10 Hz, tension, 25-220 C) showed that the temperature dependence of the moduli and the 175 C glass transition are controlled by the epoxy matrix and are independent of balloon content. Quasi-static compression of specimens cut from the graded foams showed that compressive Young's modulus (~0.5 to ~2.1 GPa) and yield stress (~20 to ~110 MPa) depend only on local density (quadratic Gibson-Ashby type relation), independently of fabrication route or mould geometry.

extraction_notes: Japanese-language paper (JSME Transactions A); quotes are verbatim Japanese. UNITS: all densities converted from kg/m3 to g/cm3 (divide by 1000). NO NUMERIC PROPERTY VALUES ARE TABULATED anywhere in this paper - compressive Young's modulus and yield stress appear only as symbols in Fig. 13 and as computed distributions in Fig. 14, and DMA E'/E''/tan delta only in log-scale Figs 10-11, so every property field is left null per the 'do not read values off plots' rule. The only text-stated property ranges are for the whole graded distribution, not per specimen: 'Young's modulus E ranges from about 0.5 GPa to about 2.1 GPa and yield stress from about 20 MPa to about 110 MPa' (Sec. 3.2.2, p. 9, computed with Eq. (1) from the density distribution of Fig. 4(a)); these were not assigned to any record. STRAIN RATE: 0.00111 1/s is derived from the stated crosshead speed of 1 mm/min on a 15 mm high specimen (1/15 per min = 1.11e-3 1/s); the paper states that the cylindrical specimens (2 mm/min, 30 mm high) were run at the same strain rate. PARTICLE SIZE: the paper gives a mean diameter range of 80-110 um for MFL-100CA rather than a single value, so particle_mean_diameter_um is left null. VOLUME FRACTION: never reported - composition is described only through density, so particle_volume_fraction is null except for the two microballoon-free epoxy specimens (S15 and the 1200 kg/m3 DMA specimen) where it is 0. CURE: cure_or_process_temperature_c = 100 C is the pre-cure (2 h); post-cure was 130 C for 15 h; the balloon-floating step was TF = 65 C for tF = 2 h (uniformly dispersed route) or TF = 50 C for tF = 50 min after 6 h of two-phase separation (two-phase route). OMITTED: graded cylindrical specimens T1 and T2 (cut from a two-phase foam of average density 930 kg/m3) were tested but neither their own densities (only Fig. 9 profiles) nor their properties (Fig. 13) are stated numerically, so no records were created for them. The density-vs-position profiles of Figs 4, 5 and 7 (foams of average density 720, 740, 840, 820 and 880 kg/m3) are structure-only figure data and were likewise not turned into records.
